Sam Harper

Game Development • Software Engineering

About Me

I'm a software engineer and game developer studying Computer Science & Engineering at The Ohio State University, with a specialization in Computer Graphics & Game Design. I like turning new and interesting ideas into reality and viewing development holistically, from concept to implementation. I pride myself on keeping a multifaceted approach to development, and blending technical expertise, creative thinking, and attention to detail to create something functional and aesthetically pleasing.

Right now I'm working as a Software Engineering Intern at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center for the summer. Outside of work and school, I play trombone as one of the fourteen members of F-row in The Ohio State University Marching Band, and I spend a lot of time playing games, reading, writing, and playing around with new ideas and technologies.

Education

The Ohio State University — B.S. Computer Science & Engineering, Computer Graphics & Game Design specialization · Expected Spring 2027

Projects

A few of my favorite projects I'd like to highlight. For the full list, see my homepage.

Dungeon Generator

A reusable Unity library for procedural tile-based dungeon generation. Built using a graph-based architecture with the goal of decoupling map topology and geometry, making it adaptable to various game genres. Features configurable room placement, guaranteed connectivity, loop injection, and reproducible seeding.

Read Full Story → GitHub

Temporal Stasis

"Can Time be stopped?" This was the theme of the 2026 Game I/O game jam at Ohio State. Over a two-week period in the midst of classes, extracurriculars, and midterm exams, my team of four developed a 2D puzzle platformer in Unity centered around freezing time. I primarily contributed as a gameplay programmer and level designer.

Read Full Story → Play on Itch.io!

Super Mario Bros. 3 Recreation

A recreation of Super Mario Bros. 3 for the Nintendo Entertainment System. Currently being made as a group project for an OSU Game Development class (CSE 3902), so the GitHub project has to stay private until its completion. Made in MonoGame and coded using C#.
